record.name: Public Housing (Community Development Authority of the City of Madison)
record.administeredBy: Community Development Authority (CDA) of the City of Madison
record.summary: Apartments owned and managed by the City of Madison's housing authority, where rent is set at about 30% of household income. Separate from the Section 8 voucher program.
record.benefit: A unit in a CDA-owned property with income-based rent (residents usually pay 30% of their income toward rent).

steps: Check the income limits and whether the public housing waitlist is open.
Apply online when the waitlist is open (accommodations available for applicants with disabilities).
Wait for a mailed notice when you reach the top of the waitlist; keep your address and household info current.

record._statusNote: 'You must apply online when the waitlist is open' -- the public housing waitlist is not continuously open. The Section 8 lottery closed April 2, 2023 and is a separate program.

of._sourceText: To qualify, your household income needs to be at or less than these federal income limits: [table] Household Size 1 = $74,800 (Public Housing column). These match HUD's 80% AMI (Low Income) limits for the Madison, WI area.
Qualify as a family as defined by the HUD and CDA.
Have at least one family member who is a citizen, national, or noncitizen with eligible immigration status. Housing assistance will be prorated ... for families that have some ineligible members.

of.note: CDA screening: criminal background check on all adults; reference and credit-history checks. Denial reasons include sex-offender registration, illegal drug use, drug-related or other criminal activity, alcohol abuse affecting tenants, lease violations / eviction filings / judgments, money owed to a landlord or federal housing authority, poor housekeeping. Not decidable from interview facts.

eligibility._note: The dollar figures are scoped by TABLE COLUMN: each row has a 'Public Housing' value and a 'Section 8' value (e.g. size 1: $74,800 public housing vs $47,400 Section 8). The two columns are two different programs with two different AMI bands (80% vs 50%). Reading the wrong column, or reading a bare number with no column, is the badgercare-plus-population-columns failure.

factsNeeded.sourceText: Qualify as a family as defined by the HUD and CDA -- a defined term with singles, elderly, disabled, and 'remaining member of a tenant family' all included; not a lay notion of 'family'

unencodable: The full CDA screening criteria (background, credit, references, landlord debt, housekeeping).
'Qualify as a family as defined by HUD and CDA' -- the HUD family definition.
Proration of assistance for mixed-status households.
Application preferences (City of Madison residents are prioritised) -- affects position, not eligibility.
The dane-ami scale in criteria.ts is modelled for the Madison MSA; the CDA table is the authority for the actual figures and would need to be checked against it, not assumed.

hops: cityofmadison.com/dpced/housing/applicants -- 'Eligibility' section carries the income table (Public Housing and Section 8 columns), the household rules, and the CDA screening criteria inline

fetch.status: HTTP 200. cityofmadison.com served fine to the desktop UA (no shell). A guessed deeper URL (/housing/eligibility-requirements/244) 404'd; the applicants page had the table anyway.

scopeColocated.scopeLocation: renderStructured kept the columns attached: 'Household Size = 1 | Public Housing = $74,800 | Section 8 = $47,400'. The scope IS the column header -- but only because the structure-preserving renderer carried it. A prose-flattened version of this page ('$74,800 ... $47,400 ...') would be exactly the badgercare-plus failure: a number with its governing column severed.

cost.notes: 1 fetch + 1 search. The Project Home Dane County Minor Home Repair page (separate candidate) turned out to publish the identical dollar table -- both are HUD 80% AMI for Dane County -- a useful cross-check that the figures are the HUD dataset.

surprises: This is the pilot's clearest live example of the column-scope failure the whole survey is trying to measure -- and it shows the fix is upstream: html-structure.ts's renderStructured() attaches the column header, so a reader working from that output cannot drop it. The failure only appears if the page is flattened first.
